gap: The build remains visibly low-poly and game-like against the official photographic bar: materials, vegetation integration, road surface detail, and atmospheric depth all need a substantial realism pass.
secondary_gaps: Terrain and distant ridges are flatter and less layered than the bar, especially in the wide vista.
Vegetation uses conspicuous billboard/cluster shapes with hard density falloff and weak ground contact.
Road markings, guardrails, and lighting lack the bar's fine-grained surface variation and contact shadows.
Cockpit geometry and dashboard framing are serviceable but materially less detailed and less photoreal.
Winter palette reads as a bright stylized snow pass rather than the bar's snow-covered, fog-layered landscape.

shots.note: B has richer photographic terrain, road, and foliage detail; A is visibly flat low-poly.
A has convincing warm exposure, road texture, car detail, and long-shadow integration; B is washed and sparse.
B has readable headlight illumination, road edge, and mountain silhouette; A is very dark with weak light response.
B has detailed cockpit controls, mirror, guardrail, and low-contrast overcast exposure; A has coarse interior geometry and foliage.
A (sr13) has snow-covered hills, fog layering, and natural road/snow blending; B is a bright flat snow overlay.
B has stronger elevated composition, ridge depth, shoreline/terrain materials, and natural vegetation scale.
A has realistic road markings, mirror, dashboard material, and windshield framing; B remains stylized and low-detail.

verdict_text: Independent fresh-headless capture at 1920x1080. All seven anonymous pairs were judged for visual quality before the A/B key was opened. The official bar won every pair; the largest gap is the rendering/material realism and integrated atmospheric depth, not a single isolated prop. winter is compared specifically against official sr_13.jpg.
